about.title: Who the f*ck is Jelly?
paragraphs: Jelly Labs was created by people who have spent years inside software delivery, recruitment and staff augmentation. We have seen what happens when sales overpromise, recruitment works without context and great engineers become rows in a spreadsheet.
So we built a simpler model: fewer layers, stronger relationships and a live view of who is genuinely ready to help.
about.signoff: We are flexible by design. Accountable by choice.

proof.title: Markets we work with.
proof.placeholderTitle: Case study — content required before launch

items.a: It is a flexible way to add external specialists to your existing team while keeping product and delivery ownership on your side.
It depends on the role and interview process. Jelly Drop highlights people whose availability has been recently confirmed.
We review experience, technical fit, communication, expectations and availability before presenting a profile. The exact technical process can be adjusted to your role.

items.q: Can you build a full team?
items.a: Yes. We can assemble dedicated or mixed teams across engineering, QA, Cloud/DevOps, Data/AI and eCommerce.
Our core network is based in Poland and Central Europe and works remotely with clients across Europe and beyond.

items.q: What happens if the match does not work?
items.a: We agree on a transparent feedback and replacement process before the engagement begins.

items.q: Do you work with software houses?
items.a: Yes. Software houses are one of our primary partner groups. We can support overflow, niche skills, urgent delivery gaps and longer-term team extension.

aboutPage.title: Flexible by design. Accountable by choice.
paragraphs: Jelly Labs connects strong technology professionals with companies that need to move without lowering their standards.
We know the staff augmentation market from the inside: sales, recruitment, delivery and the uncomfortable conversations that decide whether a partnership really works.
We created Jelly Labs because the market does not need another CV forwarding machine. It needs better context, current information and people who remain responsible after the introduction.
principles: Do not confuse urgency with chaos.
manifesto: Rigid structures break. Good teams adapt.
That does not mean standards disappear. It means the right people, information and decisions can move without unnecessary friction.
